title: Implement Min-Heap
description: Array-as-binary-heap with siftUp on push and siftDown on pop — the real priority-queue primitive behind heapsort, Dijkstra, and Top-K.

notes: Push: append at the end, then siftUp — swap with parent while parent is larger.
Pop: save root, move last element to index 0, then siftDown — swap with the SMALLER child while it is smaller.
Always swap with the smaller child on siftDown — swapping with the larger one would violate the heap property.

questions.q: Given index i, the parent index is:
On siftDown, which child do you swap with when both children are smaller than the node?
options: The smaller of the two children
questions.explain: Swapping with the larger child would leave the smaller child violating the heap property under it.

questions.q: Time complexity of push and pop?
Why move the LAST element to index 0 before siftDown on pop?
options: It keeps the underlying array contiguous so the tree shape stays complete

exercises.prompt: Fill in the MinHeap. Index math and the smaller-child pick are the load-bearing blanks.

L3.prompt: Implement a MinHeap class with push, pop, peek, and size. Push 5,3,8,1,9,2 then pop everything into an array and log `JSON.stringify` of it.
hints: Push: append at tail, then siftUp by comparing to parent at (i-1)>>1.
Pop: save a[0], move the last element to index 0, then siftDown picking the SMALLER child while it is smaller.
Popping in a loop yields ascending order — that is the heap-sort principle.
